einzeiler: Exploring the history and legacy of the Reconstruction era in America.
kurzfassung: Malcolm Gladwell introduces a new podcast series exploring the Reconstruction era in conversation with Barack Obama. The series examines how the US attempted to build a multiracial democracy after the Civil War despite immense political violence and opposition. Understanding this turbulent period provides crucial context for addressing modern democratic challenges.
stichpunkte: Barack Obama recalls being discouraged by a teacher from writing an admiring school report on Robert E. Lee.
Malcolm Gladwell reflects on his childhood in Canada and his first encounter with the legacy of American slavery.
Reconstruction is defined as the decade following the 1865 Civil War aimed at rebuilding the nation.
Congress passed the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments to abolish slavery and secure equal rights and voting access.
The era featured unprecedented Black political representation in the South at local and federal levels.
Reconstruction was not a failure, but rather was defeated by powerful forces opposing multiracial democracy.
Studying the contradictions and persistence of the past helps illuminate contemporary struggles for civil rights.

kapitel.titel: Introduction and the Myth of American History
Malcolm Gladwell's Encounter with the Legacy of Slavery
The Radical Promise and Political Violence of Reconstruction
Defeat, Memory, and Lessons for Today

clips.hook: Writing a school report on Robert E. Lee
clips.text: As a schoolboy, the future president was steered away from writing a praiseful assignment about a Confederate general who fought to preserve slavery.

clips.hook: Thousands of proposed amendments, very few passed
clips.text: Out of more than 11,000 proposed changes to the founding document, only 27 have ever been successfully enacted.

clips.hook: A radical shift from states' rights to federal enforcement
clips.text: The traditional dominance of local jurisdiction was upended by shifting the power of law enforcement directly to the federal government.

clips.hook: Unprecedented Black political power in the South
clips.text: Numerous Black officials successfully attained political office across various levels of government during this transformative post-war period.
The historical period is properly characterized not as an inherent failure, but rather as an ambitious project that was actively defeated.

beschreibung:
If you loved The Wonder of Stevie, you can’t miss Higher Ground and Audible’s newest series, Reconstruction: The Unfinished Promise.
Reconstruction was a time when Americans struggled over fundamental questions about our country. Who gets to be a citizen? Who has the right to vote? Who can own property? In short, who belongs? Best-selling author and host of Revisionist History, Malcolm Gladwell, guides us through this extraordinary moment in American history with help from former President Barack Obama. Together they explore why America has yet to make good on the promise of Reconstruction — and how it still might.
